title: The Road In
goal: Every player has said how their own character got here and one thing about who they were the day before this letter arrived.
howToPlay: A montage, not a scene. Cut fast between six short spotlights, a minute or two each, then stop. This is the only stretch all session where each of them is, for a moment, the only person on screen. Do not have them meet each other here -- the waiting room next scene is the first time this group is a group, on purpose, and it lands harder for being held back one beat longer.

intro.where: Six separate mornings, six separate places. Weeks ago, each of them got the same letter.
intro.firstThing: An envelope from a city none of them had reason to visit, addressed correctly, from an institution that has never written to them before.
intro.readAloud:
Dear Candidate,

Your application to the City Civil Defence Directorate has been reviewed and accepted. You are asked to report to the combined campus no later than Monday next, where you will be issued instructions, quartered, and enrolled.

Please bring nothing you cannot carry, and nothing you cannot leave.

We look forward to your service.

carriesIn.when: This is the campaign's first played scene
carriesIn.then: Nothing carries in yet. This is everyone's first impression of their own character, and it should be entirely theirs to make.

beats.text: Read the letter once, to the whole table, before anyone speaks as their character.
beats.readAloud:
Dear Candidate,

Your application to the City Civil Defence Directorate has been reviewed and accepted. You are asked to report to the combined campus no later than Monday next, where you will be issued instructions, quartered, and enrolled.

Please bring nothing you cannot carry, and nothing you cannot leave.

We look forward to your service.
beats.direction: It is the same letter all six of them got, weeks apart, from a city none of them had reason to visit. Say nothing else about it. Let the table sit with "nothing you cannot leave" for a second before moving on -- it is doing real work and does not need to be pointed at.

beats.text: Go round the table. Ask each player directly: how do you get here, and what's the last thing that happens before you arrive?
beats.direction: Ask first. Only offer an example if a player is stuck -- it's a nudge, not a menu, and should never look like six pre-assigned slots. Keep each spotlight short, one exchange, unless a player is clearly enjoying it: six of these can eat the session if you let each one run long.
beats.note: IF SOMEBODY WANTS AN EXAMPLE: "Arrived on a battered motorbike that shouldn't still run, and does." / "Took the early commuter train in with forty strangers going nowhere else." / "Drove an old banger that needed pushing the last hundred yards." / "Walked the causeway on foot, because the fare wasn't worth what it cost." / "Came in by boat with the morning catch, because that's who was going that way." / "Hitched the last leg with someone who never once asked why." These are inspiration, not a script -- a player's own idea always wins.

beats.text: If a player's arrival has an obvious moment in it, offer one roll, their choice of skill.

when.condition: if a player's own arrival has something worth rolling for

beats.note: Never required. This costs nothing on any result -- it exists to make an entrance a little more vivid, not to gate it. Plenty of good arrivals have nothing to roll for at all.

beats.text: Somewhere on a fence line one of them passes, easy to miss: a small wire trap with a coin bounty tag on it, identical to the rat traps twenty feet further along.

when.condition: if anyone's arrival passes it, or if anyone asks what it's for

beats.direction: Don't call attention to it. This is an Encyclopaedia check (design/encyclopaedia-checks.md) -- offer it freely if it comes up, never force it.
beats.note: PLANT -- mystery ledger #1 for the mitflit trail, design/induction.md. The first thing any of them ever sees of a mitflit, and it should read as absolutely nothing, whether or not anyone rolls.

outro.endsWhen: All six spotlights are done. Stop there -- do not stage a shared arrival or have them notice each other. That's next scene's opening, not this one's ending.
outro.onwards: Straight into Intake Medicals. Time skips a few days on its own -- that scene opens already inside the queue, and this is where the six of them actually become a group for the first time.
writeDown: How each character arrived, worth one callback later if it fits naturally.
Whether anyone noticed the trap on the fence, and what they decided it was for.

notes: Deliberately no shared beat and no artefact. The group forming is Intake Medicals' job, stated in its own queue beat and confirmed 2026-09-09 as intentional -- this scene must not spend that moment early. Assumes character sheets already exist (built at session zero, before this is ever played) -- the flourish check has real stats to roll against from the first line.
